title: Counting phase of the split-search round
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $start$ be one of its states, and let $w,s$ be Boolean words and $out$ a Boolean word. If, from the source configuration with state $start$, all work tapes containing the unary word of length $|s|+1$, heads at position $0$, and empty output, the source machine on empty input reaches the halted configuration with the same unary work tapes and output $out$ after $T$ steps, then there is a time $t\le T$ at which the split-search round body on input $w$, started from the counting-host configuration embedding the source's initial configuration, reaches the corresponding embedding of the halted configuration with output $out$. At every time from $0$ through $t$, the round body avoids its anchor state.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
The source run from the specified unary-tape initial configuration halts after $T$ steps with output $out$ and the same work tapes
